name: American Beech

facts.where: Rich woods of far East Texas

caution: Sweet and good in moderation; very large quantities of raw beechnuts can disagree, so roast and enjoy them as a treat. Never eat a wild plant on this guide's word alone. Confirm identity against several sources and learn the look-alikes first.

sections.title: Harvesting
sections.body: Smooth gray bark and coppery fall leaves mark the beech. Its little three-sided nuts hide in soft burrs.

sections.title: In the kitchen
sections.body: Fiddly to shell but genuinely delicious, best lightly roasted.
